explanations.explanation: Two withouts, one right after the other! Isaiah 55:1 offers wine and milk "without money and without cost!" That's not a sale, that's a giveaway.

Delay? Nope, this blank is all about the price. Isaiah 55:1 calls out to the thirsty, then to "you without money," and the LORD offers wine and milk with no money and no cost at all. Free, free, and then FREE again. My kind of checkout line.

Ooh, "without end" has a nice ring to it, I'll give you that. But this verse is talking price tags, and there isn't one. Wine and milk, no money, no cost, all in Isaiah 55:1. If I ran my bakery like that, my cash register would get lonely.

Isaiah 55:2 asks why spend money on what is not bread, and then the LORD gives the fix: "Listen carefully to Me, and eat what is good, and your soul will delight in the richest of foods." Quit chasing what leaves you empty and come listen. It's like scrolling for an hour looking for something good when the good thing was sitting right there the whole time.

Look again, this one's actually true. The LORD doesn't stop at asking why they labor on what does not satisfy. He tells them what to do instead, and His very next words in Isaiah 55:2 tell them to listen carefully to Him. Do that, and their soul will delight in the richest of foods. The fix for empty isn't trying harder. It's listening to Him.

David, Israel's king, is the man named in Isaiah 55:3, where the LORD speaks of "My loving devotion promised to David." Verse 4 keeps going about him: "Behold, I have made him a witness to the nations, a leader and commander of the peoples." The LORD put a name on this promise, and it's David's. Me, I only got my name carved on a handle.

Not Moses this time. Moses, Israel's leader, never comes up in this passage. In Isaiah 55:3 the LORD ties the covenant to "My loving devotion promised to David." That's David, Israel's king. Moses will have to sit in the back for this one, and trust me, I know all about sitting in the back.

Here's the twist: Abraham, the forefather of Israel, isn't named anywhere in this passage. The name in Isaiah 55:3 belongs to David, Israel's king, because the LORD speaks of His loving devotion promised to David. Then verse 4 stays right on him, calling him a witness to the nations. One name on this promise, and it's David's.

Witness, leader, AND commander. In Isaiah 55:4 the LORD says, "Behold, I have made him a witness to the nations, a leader and commander of the peoples." Three titles! Meanwhile my title is "guy who packs boxes with his face."

Easy to miss, because the witness part comes first. But in Isaiah 55:4 the LORD keeps going: "a leader and commander of the peoples." So David gets the whole set, witness, leader and commander. That is a LOT of name tags for one shirt.

explanations.answer: Their God has made them glorious
explanations.explanation: Isaiah 55:5 gives the reason right there: "For the LORD your God, the Holy One of Israel, has bestowed glory on you." Look at that word "bestowed." The glory is a gift from God, and because of it, nations come RUNNING to this people. Me, I only run for the oven timer.

explanations.answer: Their armies have made them strong
explanations.explanation: Armies get a nation noticed, sure. But Isaiah 55:5 doesn't mention a single soldier. The nations come running because the LORD their God, the Holy One of Israel, has bestowed glory on them. That's God's gift, not anybody's muscle.

explanations.answer: Their trade has made them rich
explanations.explanation: Money talks, I know, but not in this verse. Isaiah 55:5 says the draw is glory, and it's the LORD their God, the Holy One of Israel, who gave it to them. Funny thing is, this whole chapter opened back in verse 1 with buying "without money and without cost!" Riches were never the point here.

No fine print on this one. Isaiah 55:7 says to return to the LORD, "that He may have compassion, and to our God, for He will freely pardon." FREELY. No processing fee. No "please hold, your pardon is important to us."

Too good to be true? Not here. Isaiah 55:7 ends with "for He will freely pardon." It calls the wicked man to forsake his way and return to the LORD, "that He may have compassion," and that's a promise worth coming home to. Believe me, an old stamper who spent years behind the takeout menus knows how good it feels when somebody reaches in for you.

Think about how far the sky is above your head. That's the gap the LORD describes in Isaiah 55:9: "For as the heavens are higher than the earth, so My ways are higher than your ways and My thoughts than your thoughts." Me, I can barely reach the top shelf over my ovens.

Older sounds wise, but the picture here is all about height. The LORD measures it against the sky: "as the heavens are higher than the earth" (Isaiah 55:9). His ways and thoughts sit that far above ours. Look up, way up, and you've got it.

Ha! Simpler would be nice, wouldn't it? But in Isaiah 55:9 the LORD says His ways and thoughts are higher than theirs, just as the heavens are higher than the earth. Higher, WAY up there. Good thing, too, because I once spent twenty minutes looking for the spatula I was holding with my own mustache.

The LORD finishes the picture in Isaiah 55:11: "so My word that proceeds from My mouth will not return to Me empty, but it will accomplish what I please, and it will prosper where I send it." Rain comes down, the earth buds and sprouts, and the job gets done. His word works just like that.

Tears don't show up anywhere in this passage, friend. The rain picture points to something the LORD sends out, and in Isaiah 55:11 it's the word that proceeds from His mouth. Rain doesn't go back without watering the earth, and His word won't come back empty either. Every drop counts.

So close, because rain and fields really do go together! But the thing being compared comes in Isaiah 55:11, where the LORD says the word that proceeds from His mouth will not return to Him empty. The rain is the picture. His word is the point.

Other way around! Empty is the one thing His word will NOT do. The LORD says it "will not return to Me empty, but it will accomplish what I please" (Isaiah 55:11). Me, I send a batch into the oven and sometimes it comes back as charcoal. His word? Never.

His word goes out and gets the job done. In the LORD's own words in Isaiah 55:11, it will "accomplish what I please, and it will prosper where I send it." Not empty. Not halfway. I wish my first thousand cookie stamps had that kind of track record.

Mountains. Singing. In Isaiah 55:12 the LORD says, "You will indeed go out with joy and be led forth in peace; the mountains and hills will burst into song before you, and all the trees of the field will clap their hands." I can't carry a tune past the mixing bowl, and here come the HILLS harmonizing.

Not this time! This is a joyful parade. In Isaiah 55:12 the LORD says they will go out with joy and be led forth in peace, and the mountains and hills will "burst into song" before them. No shaking here, just a hillside choir.

Melting is a cookie problem, friend, not a mountain problem, at least not here. In Isaiah 55:12 the LORD says the mountains and hills will "burst into song" as they go out with joy. This whole scene is joy and peace. Let's leave the melting to my chocolate chips.

Flip it! In Isaiah 55:13 the LORD says that instead of the thornbush, the cypress will grow, and instead of the brier, the myrtle will spring up. The thorns are on their way OUT. It's like tossing a burnt batch and pulling a perfect one out of the oven.

Out with the prickly stuff! In Isaiah 55:13 the thornbush and the brier get replaced. The cypress grows where the thornbush was, and the myrtle springs up where the brier was. Honestly, that's the most satisfying swap since my crooked stamps finally came out straight.

Cypress where the thornbush was, myrtle where the brier was, and Isaiah 55:13 says this will make a name for the LORD that lasts. It's "an everlasting sign, never to be destroyed." Every cookie I've ever stamped is long gone. This sign sticks around FOREVER.
Oh, this one goes the long way! In Isaiah 55:13 the LORD calls it "an everlasting sign, never to be destroyed." Temporary is a plate of my cookies sitting in front of me. This sign lasts forever.
Hidden? Not this sign! Picture cypress and myrtle growing right where the thornbush and brier used to be. Isaiah 55:13 says this will make a name for the LORD. That's not a secret. That's a sign.
